summary: Carefully executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator against the same validator plus sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks (Npairs=720). Results show near-ceiling validator coverage (baseline 719/720, guarded 720/720), a vanishing paired gain (0.00139), and non-significant McNemar result (p=1.0). The run appears methodologically rigorous and reproducible from archived artifacts, but the manuscript requires a small set of editorial and disclosure fixes before finalisation.
critical_issues: Manuscript uses raw URLs/arXiv/hdl identifiers in prose rather than standard IEEE-numbered inline citation markers; inline citation format must be converted to IEEE numbered markers and the reference list must contain full verified bibliographic entries matching those markers.

The Disclosure Statement presently includes run-internal paths, detailed manifest entries, and full hashes in manuscript text. Per track guidance, condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise summary (models/tools used, preregistration id and checksum, master-prompt reference, human/autonomy boundary, and archival availability of the full execution manifest) and move per-file provenance details to the archived artifact bundle rather than ordinary prose.

Although the manuscript already records shared_initial_candidate semantics in some places, ensure Methods and Results explicitly and prominently state that the same single initial model generation was reused across the paired conditions and clarify the implications (i.e., discordance could only arise from guarded-stage emulation observations or the single repair call).
required_revisions: Replace all inline citations in the manuscript body with IEEE numbered markers and populate the References section with full, verified IEEE-style entries (use the archived verified bibliography artifacts). Ensure each numbered citation in prose directly supports the adjacent claim; correct any mismatches using the archived bibliography.

Condense the Disclosure Statement within pages 1–5 to the concise mandatory content (model identifiers, orchestration/validator names, preregistration id and its SHA‑256, master-prompt reference, human role/autonomy boundary, statement that full execution/manifest artifacts are archived and retrievable). Remove per-file paths, execution-log excerpts, and routine artifact hashes from the main manuscript text; retain those details only in the archived evidence bundle referenced by the Disclosure.

Add one clear, explicit sentence in Methods and re-state in Results that the experiment used shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) and explain the effect of that design choice on possible sources of discordance (i.e., only guarded-stage emulation observations or the single repair call could create between-condition differences).
optional_revisions: Optionally report the preregistered exploratory per-class and per-vendor paired summaries (already present in the archived artifacts) as a short table or sentence to help readers assess heterogeneity, provided no new analyses beyond archived artifacts are introduced.

Optionally include a short illustrative example (one representative discordant task) drawn from the archived artifacts to concretely demonstrate how the validator and the emulator behaved on a discordant or near-discordant case.
Optionally shorten or tighten background/related-work wording to free space for the concise Disclosure Statement and the explicit shared_initial_candidate clarification if page budget is tight.
